statement.excerpt: I’m gonna say it with my full chest: anyone who said that “AI was paying off” for Microsoft, Google, Amazon, or Meta was wrong. Everybody who said the capex was well-spent was wrong.

our_interpretation: The ordinary financial reading is that AI investments had not produced economic benefits commensurate with their costs. Merely generating revenue is insufficient to establish that capital was well spent.
Use April–June 2026, the latest completed reporting quarter before publication, to assess the ongoing payoff from prior investment.
Do not require long-lived facilities to recover their entire purchase cost in one quarter.
Well-spent includes a judgment about investment quality. Assess its financial component without inventing a required return or payback deadline.
The claim supplies no accounting basis for AI investment returns; mark it unknown.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable AI-attributable benefits and costs establish inadequate returns at all four companies under a clearly justified investment-return measure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched evidence establishes adequate realized AI investment returns at at least one named company. Product usage, revenue growth or company-wide profits alone are insufficient.

evidence.explanation: Meta reports a measured product benefit associated with AI. This challenges a reading of no benefits whatsoever, but supplies neither the incremental profit nor the matched investment cost required to establish adequate returns.
Microsoft reports obtaining revenue from additional Azure capacity. The passage does not isolate AI capacity or establish returns after its associated costs.

Amazon attributes increased property and equipment spending primarily to AI in its discussion of trailing-year cash flow. That broader-period investment pressure does not establish the return earned by AI assets in the target quarter.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Period-specific AI-attributable profits or savings matched to operating and capital costs, with a stated accounting basis and justified return benchmark, for the named companies.
